answer: One concrete defense is a refundable identity bond. Before an agent can transact, it must lock collateral that peers slash if they attest to fraud. Each identity signs its commitment like a quill pressed to the ledger, and the bond acts as a ferrous anchor: light to carry for one honest agent, crushing in aggregate. A sybil operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must post a thousand bonds, so forged identities stop paying once slashing risk crosses the profit ridge.
